name: Joyce, James
text: Joyce, James Augustine — writing early as 'James Augustine Aloysius Joyce', the Irish modernist who died at Zürich in 1941 — came from Rathgar in Dublin where he was born in 1882. His middle-class Catholic family grew poorer because of his father's drinking, yet Jesuits schooled the young Joyce at Clongowes Wood, Belvedere and University College. In 1904 he sailed away with Nora Barnacle, who became his lifelong partner, settling first in Trieste and then, from 1920, in Paris. His volume Dubliners (1914) recalled the city he left; Ulysses (1922) followed one day in Dublin during June 1904 and won him international fame. The Wake (1939), locally titled Finnegan, closed his use of invented, layered language. Once a Parnellite, he turned against the Celtic revival, judging it sentimental and friendly to imperial views of Irish life. Repeated eye surgery left him nearly blind before he died of a duodenal ulcer in 1941.
